page: Microsoft Azure D4lds_v7 is a compute-optimized virtual machine from the Dldsv7 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical Intel Xeon 6973P-C cores with hyper-threading enabled. Operating at a high clock speed of 4.2 GHz, this x86_64 processor includes a massive 480 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache. The instance is configured with a low-memory profile of 8.0 GB RAM (2.0 GB per core) and includes 236 GB of local disk storage with Premium Storage capabilities.

In benchmark evaluations, the D4lds_v7 demonstrates strong single-threaded performance, particularly in data compression tasks, with gzip compression reaching 36.23 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 14.92 GB/sec. However, multi-threaded performance is relatively weak, as evidenced by a stress-ng multi-core score of 4655.9 and a multi-threaded bzip3 decompression rate of 29.51 GB/sec. Memory bandwidth is average for read operations, peaking at 345.13 GB/sec for cached small blocks, but drops to a weak 23.53 GB/sec for large-block write operations. For database and web workloads, the server delivers average throughput, achieving 8.31 million operations per second in Redis SET tests and 8.67 GB/sec in static web serving.

The primary tradeoff of the D4lds_v7 is its constrained memory capacity of 8.0 GB, which limits its suitability for memory-intensive applications or large-scale LLM inference, where 7B model text generation drops to a poor 4.86 tokens/sec. Qualitatively, the instance offers a cost-effective option for compute-bound workloads that do not require large memory footprints, leveraging its high 4.2 GHz clock speed and advanced instruction sets like AVX-512 and AMX. It is best suited for single-threaded processing tasks, lightweight web serving, basic database operations, and entry-level containerized microservices.
